audit.whatIsWrong: Three separate errors about Rebuttal (W). The page calls it a dash or 'short W reposition' in four places — Riot's text describes a barrier that reflects projectiles, prevents her from taking damage and grants movement speed. Mel has no dash in her kit at all. Second, whys[2] and spikes[1] assert that a stun 'cannot be reflected by her W'; Rebuttal reflects projectiles and Flawless Duet is flagged as a projectile, so that is a confident claim I cannot verify from the kits and it points the player straight into the barrier. Third, its cooldown — 38 seconds at rank 1 — is never given, despite being by far the most punishable cooldown in the lane. The R is also called 'Overwhelm' when Overwhelm is the passive's stacking debuff; the ultimate is Golden Eclipse.
audit.why: Rebuttal prevents damage outright. Telling a player her stun goes through it invites her to spend E, R and her whole commit into a two-second immunity window on a 38-second cooldown — the exact opposite of the correct play, which is to bait it.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal described as what it is, with its 38s rank-1 cooldown, and every 'W dash' replaced. The reflect claim is removed rather than reversed — the page now says bait it, which is right either way. Golden Eclipse named correctly.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[1], early and late all deploy Defiant Dance (W) as the answer to Mel's poke. The mel__irelia mirror already established that Defiant Dance mitigates physical damage and heals nothing, so it is dead weight against Mel — and charging it stops Irelia moving, which is worse than useless against a 950-range zone. The page also calls Ionian Fervor an armour/MR shred in four places; it is stacking attack speed plus on-hit damage.
audit.why: Stating the same fact from this side keeps the two pages consistent: the mirror tells Mel that Irelia charging W has stopped threatening her, so this page must not tell Irelia that charging W protects her.
audit.corrected: Defiant Dance removed as a defensive answer in whys[1], early and late; all four shred claims replaced with the attack-speed stacking Riot's text describes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 read Mel in both layers while whys[4] and spikes[2] both call it your premier dive window, and the packet chart gives it to Irelia.
audit.why: The mirror's chart finding is 'Level 1 is Mel's; the rest of the chart stays with Irelia'. Leaving Level 6 as Mel here would put the two pages in direct contradiction on a 57.87% matchup.
audit.corrected: phases[4].side and win[4] flipped to Irelia as a matched pair, rating raised from 3/10 to 7/10. Level 1 stays Mel, everything else already matched.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page tracks Solar Snare as the matchup-defining cooldown and never gives a number for it or for anything else.
audit.why: Solar Snare is 11s at rank 1 and Rebuttal is 38s — the second is the one worth waiting for, and the page pointed the reader at the first.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal's 38s written into whys[2] and mid as the real punish window.

edits.before: Your W (Defiant Dance) channel soaks her poke and lets you trade back, but without E you still can't lock her down to punish — the window is even.
edits.after: Defiant Dance does nothing here — her damage is magic — and with no E to lock her down, just deny CS and bank passive stacks. Even window.

edits.before: E-stun into a Q-reset is your first all-in, and a stun cannot be reflected by her W (Rebuttal) — one combo halves a Mel who can't kite a locked-down dash.
edits.after: E-stun into a Q-reset is your first all-in, but bait Rebuttal first — it prevents damage outright and reflects projectiles, and it is 38 seconds at rank 1.

edits.before: Your max-stack Bladesurge passive comes online to shred her armor/MR and your reset tightens — you out-skirmish her poke and heal through it once you're in melee.
edits.after: Your max-stack passive comes online — attack speed and on-hit damage, not shred — and your resets tighten, so you out-skirmish her poke once you're in melee.

edits.before: Your Trinity Force spike gives full reset uptime and passive shred — gap close on her Q cooldown and her squishy mage frame can't survive it.
edits.after: Your Trinity Force spike gives full reset uptime and max attack speed — close on her Q cooldown and her squishy mage frame can't survive it.

edits.before: She stays squishy with only a short W dash to escape, and your wall denies even that — keep forcing the all-in and end before her R (Overwhelm) execute scales into a one-shot.
edits.after: She stays squishy and has no dash at all — Rebuttal only buys her seconds — so keep forcing the all-in and end before her Golden Eclipse (R) execute scales into a one-shot.

edits.before: E (Flawless Duet) stun into Bladesurge reset is your first real all-in — a stun ignores her W reflect, so once the blades clamp she gets walked down with no answer.
edits.after: E (Flawless Duet) stun into Bladesurge reset is your first real all-in — but wait out Rebuttal, which stops damage and reflects projectiles, then clamp her with no answer left.

edits.before: Trinity Force spike: full Bladesurge reset uptime plus passive armor/MR shred — gap close on her Q cooldown and her squishy mage frame folds before W comes back up.
edits.after: Trinity Force spike: full Bladesurge reset uptime plus max Ionian Fervor attack speed — close on her Q cooldown and her mage frame folds long before Rebuttal returns.

edits.before: Reposition out on her W dash and look for an R (Overwhelm) execute when you dive in low
edits.after: Ride your commit out inside Rebuttal, then execute you with Golden Eclipse when you dive low

edits.before: Mel owns the very first window — her Q (Radiant Volley) poke outranges everything you have at level 1, so concede the screen and just last-hit, accepting some chip. Level 2 gives you W (Defiant Dance), the damage-reduction channel to soak her harder pokes, so step up and bank Bladesurge passive stacks. Critically, do NOT throw a Q at a minion in her face: she can Rebuttal-reflect it or simply step back and Q you for free. Wait until you have E so your dash actually leads into a stun.
edits.after: Mel owns the very first window — her Q (Radiant Volley) poke outranges everything you have at level 1, so concede the screen and just last-hit, accepting some chip. Don't count on Defiant Dance at 2: it reduces physical damage and hers is magic, and charging it means you have stopped moving inside a 950-range zone. Critically, do NOT throw a Q at a minion in her face — she steps back and Q's you for free. Wait for E so your dash leads into a stun.

edits.before: This is your takeover. At 3 your E (Flawless Duet) stun into Bladesurge reset finally lets you reach her, and here's the key: her W (Rebuttal) reflects projectiles and reduces incoming damage, but it does nothing against a stun or a gap-closing dash — so once your blades connect she can't punish your commit. Bait the Rebuttal with a fake step-up, and when it's down, E-stun, Q-reset off her, and let your max-stack passive shred her squishy frame. At 6 Vanguard's Edge walls her against terrain so she can't reposition out while you run her down — but watch her R (Overwhelm) if you both go low.
edits.after: This is your takeover. At 3 your E (Flawless Duet) stun into Bladesurge reset finally lets you reach her, but here's the key: Rebuttal prevents her taking damage at all and reflects projectiles, so anything you spend into it is gone. Bait it with a fake step-up — it is 38 seconds at rank 1, so once it's spent the lane is yours for two full waves. Then E-stun, Q-reset off her, and let your max-stack attack speed do the work on a frame with no dash in it. At 6 Vanguard's Edge cuts her escape lane and pins her against terrain, but watch Golden Eclipse if you both go low.

edits.before: You stay favoured into the late game — Mel is a squishy ranged mage whose only escape is the short W reposition, and once you're on her your reset chain plus your wall denies it. The real danger is letting her free-poke from max Q range in teamfights, or diving in low and eating an R (Overwhelm) execute as it scales harder the lower you are. Use Vanguard's Edge to cut her off from her team, save your W to soak the burst she reflects back, and close before she stacks enough AP to delete you on the approach.
edits.after: You stay favoured into the late game — Mel is a squishy ranged mage with no dash at all, so once you're on her, your reset chain plus the wall ends it. The real danger is letting her free-poke from max Q range in teamfights, or diving in low and eating a Golden Eclipse execute that scales with every Overwhelm stack she has put on you. Use Vanguard's Edge to cut her off from her team, never spend a commit into an active Rebuttal, and close before her AP deletes you on the approach.

notes: Rebuttal was described as a dash in four places — Mel has no dash; it is a barrier that prevents damage, reflects projectiles and grants move speed, on a 38-second rank-1 cooldown that the page never mentioned. The page also asserted that Irelia's stun cannot be reflected by it; Flawless Duet is flagged as a projectile in her own kit, so I removed that claim rather than reversing it — see questionsForUser. Defiant Dance was again offered as protection against magic damage, matching the error the mel__irelia mirror already corrected from the other side, and Ionian Fervor was called shred four more times. Level 6 flipped to Irelia in both layers to agree with the packet, the prose, and the mirror. The R was called 'Overwhelm' throughout; Overwhelm is the passive's stack, the ultimate is Golden Eclipse.
